title: Boundary Criticality in (2+1)-dimensional U(1) Dirac Quantum Spin Liquid
authors: Huan Jiang, Zhiming Pan, Xue-Jia Yu, Shao-Kai Jian
abstract: An emergent gauge field can control boundary critical behavior without changing the bulk quantum spin liquid. We investigate the boundary criticality in $(2+1)$-dimensional $U(1)$ Dirac spin liquid, whose low-energy physics is described by massless quantum electrodynamics. Using a perturbative renormalization-group analysis in a half-space, we show that Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions for the emergent gauge field lead to distinct boundary universality classes. We determine the boundary scaling dimensions of the fundamental fields and gauge-invariant operators that provide observable signatures. We further propose a fermion-gauge lattice model with tunable boundary interactions as a microscopic setting for realizing and probing these boundary universality classes.
summary: This work analyzes the boundary criticality of a 2+1 dimensional U(1) Dirac Quantum Spin Liquid using perturbative Renormalization Group techniques. By examining the difference between Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions, the authors establish that these conditions define distinct boundary universality classes. The findings are supported by a proposed fermion-gauge lattice model for potential physical realization.
main_problem: The paper investigates the boundary criticality in a (2+1)-dimensional U(1) Dirac Quantum Spin Liquid (QSL).
main_result: The boundary conditions (Neumann vs. Dirichlet) lead to distinct boundary universality classes, characterized by different boundary scaling dimensions.
method: The analysis employs a perturbative Renormalization-Group (RG) approach in a half-space, calculating one-loop corrections to boundary two-point functions.
model_or_system: The system is a U(1) Dirac spin liquid, whose low-energy physics is modeled by (2+1) dimensional Quantum Electrodynamics (QED$_3$). A microscopic lattice model is also proposed to realize these boundary interactions.
key_observables: Boundary scaling dimensions ($\Delta_\partial$), boundary renormalization factors ($Z_\partial$), and the anomalous dimension of boundary fermion operators ($\eta_\partial^O$).
important_parameters: The gauge coupling constant ($e$), the dimensionality (2+1), and the boundary conditions (Neumann/Dirichlet).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to one-loop order and relies on the continuum QED$_3$ description of the QSL.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the electrostatic image-charge picture for boundary conditions, one-loop diagrams for renormalization, and the structure of the proposed fermion-gauge lattice model.
paper_structure: The paper develops the RG analysis by calculating bulk and boundary renormalization factors for fermion and gauge fields, determines the boundary scaling dimensions based on boundary conditions, and concludes by proposing a lattice realization.
why_interesting: The study of boundary effects in strongly correlated systems like QSLs is crucial for understanding how boundaries modify bulk quantum phases, which is relevant for engineered quantum materials.

(b,c) Electrostatic image-charge picture of the Neumann (b) and Dirichlet (c) boundary conditions, corresponding to same-sign and opposite-sign image charges, respectively.

FIG. 2. One-loop diagrams for the boundary renormalization of (a) the fermion self-energy, (b) the gauge field polarization, and (c) the fermion composite operator. All external legs terminate on the boundary, as indicated by ◦. The solid line with arrow denotes the fermion propagator, while the waving line represents the gauge field porpagator. The □represents a composite operator insertion on the boundary.

The system has open boundary conditions along the x di- rection and periodic boundary conditions along the y axis. Gray (white) sites denote A (B) sublattices. The hopping amplitude between A sublattice (pink link) is −t, and t oth- erwise. The dashed virtual bonds contain the boundary- localized U(1) phase field φi.
